title: His first band: the seven-piece group at Detroit's Savoy
summary: He led a seven-piece band playing stock arrangements of tunes like China Boy and Tiger Rag for about a year before moving to New York.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You went back to Birmingham, and you played in the theatre there for a while. Then eventually, it seems you went into...you took your own band...you got your own band together. Did that happen after Charlie Creath?
That was Detroit.
Yeah.
That was Detroit I had to get my own band.
That was before or after Charlie Creath that you got this band of yours together?
I had my own band in Detroit.
Yes.
That was before.
That was before Charlie Creath. I see. Okay. So you were playing there at the Savoy. What were some of the numbers that you played with your band, and who were the members of your band?
Well, we played numbers like 'China Boy,' 'I Got Rhythm,' 'Tiger Rag,' 'Sweet Georgia Brown'... I'll tell you, 'Sweet Georgia Brown,' the guy who wrote that number, he passed away...
Moore (II) - 14
How many pieces did you... You had seven pieces in the band.
Yeah, seven pieces.
What was the instrumentation?
Piano, drums, bass, saxophones, trombone, piano...no, trumpet... Yeah, trumpet, trombone, two sax...
Two saxophones. Who were these musicians? Do you recall?
No, I don't recall their names. They were from Detroit.
From Detroit. But this was your first band as an adult, your first band that you were leading?
Yeah, my first band.
How did you feel, being the leader of a group at that time?

Well, I felt all right, because I was kind of young, but I knew what's going on. I knew how to pick my musicians, you know, and what numbers to play. We was playing numbers that we didn't have no arrangements. We just had what they called stocks, the stock music. You'd buy them at the store. At that time you could get stock music for 20 cents, 25 cents, 15 cents. And we'd read all that music, you know.
Moore (II) - 15
So no one in the band wrote any arrangements for that music. You just left it to the stocks...
No, we didn't have no arrangements. Just the stocks.
None at all.
We only had the stocks.
How long did you work with your band in Detroit at the Savoy?
About a year.
Well, it was a good year. And then what happened? Did that job close down, or did you decide to...?
No, I decided I'm gonna come to New York.
That was when you came to New York.
Yes.
